issue.title: Do not subscribe to Redis channels when results are ignored
issue.body:
## Description

The unnecessary channel subscriptions were occurring in two cases: 
- `backends.base.Backend.on_task_call` was being called unconditionally, which initiated the PubSub subscription.
- `AsyncBackendMixin.add_pending_result` also initiates a subscription.

The code excerpt given in #4707 was executed and produced no channel leak, neither on the worker nor on the consumer. Both `chord` and `AsyncResult` return values are retrieved correctly.

- [x] Avoid consumer Redis channel subscriptions if result is to be ignored.
- [x] Calling `AsyncResult.get()` now returns `None` directly, instead of subscribing to Redis channel.

Fixes #4707.

body: @bartloop if possible, please provide some feedback on the potential fix. Thank you!

@georgepsarakis Thank you much for the speedy resolution to this bug.

I do not know this code base very well, so I cannot comment on whether your fix is the right one. At the high level, your choice to avoid the subscription in the first place seems like the right solution to me.

I confirm that the fix works for me locally. If ignore_result=True, channel count stays at 0; if ignore_result=False, it grows as before.

One downside I see is that the current setup requires a fully-informed developer. Had this bug already been fixed, I would have still encountered the same problem: I did not know ignore_result was needed; I did not know that pubsub was subscribing to things in the background; and I did know that pubsub kept resubscribing to old stale channels. In fact, we ran many machines in production for several months before we noticed this. The natural assumption of a developer is "if I want a result, I need to get it; if I don't want a result, do nothing."

I do not have a solution for this downside, but since you know the code, you may have an easy solution in mind. Perhaps it is possible to detect that a task has no return value and set ignore_result automatically.

Second, because ignore_result is a task annotation rather than a parameter to apply_async, the current setup does not allow one task caller to consume a return value and another to ignore it. Of course, there are ways around this, so not a huge deal.

Again, thank you for resolving this!

@bartloop thanks for testing and providing feedback. If results are not ignored, the caller must call `result.get()` in order to unsubscribe. This is expected behavior and concerns the process that creates the tasks and consumes the results, since they must be notified that the task is ready and the result is available. Messages are forwarded only to active channels, so the subscription cannot be performed at any other time. As far as I can see, this would create an issue only if you have very long-running processes that create large numbers of tasks and never consuming the results. Ignoring results that are not going to be used is also recommended in the [documentation](http://docs.celeryproject.org/en/latest/userguide/tasks.html#ignore-results-you-don-t-want).

I noticed that the consumer does not unsubscribe when `AsyncResult.forget` is called or when the `AsyncResult` instance is deleted (using `del`), so we may need to correct this as well. In that case, the caller can simply call `forget()` instead of `get()` when they want to discard the result.
@bartloop if you think that the documentation can be expanded, to help avoid similar issues in the future, please feel free to open a Pull Request.

issue.title: Add doc warnings to ensure devs understand backend resource usage
issue.body:
Per request by @georgepsarakis on Issue #4707, I am suggesting improvements to the documentation about Task Results and backends.

Specifically, I am suggesting that warnings be added to ensure developers understand they must process task return values to avoid resource issues.

From my direct experience, the resource being consumed was redis subscriptions. "Unsubscribe" does not occur unless the caller explicitly cleans it up by calling AsynchResult.get() or AsynchResult.forget(). I am assuming (but have no direct evidence) that this is a problem with other backend providers; therefore, I have not made the documentation specific to Redis.

I chose to add these information as warnings because there are severe consequences if the developer does not take the suggested action. In fact, the problem remains hidden, possibly for weeks or months, until the redis subscription list grows to an unmanageable level.

I chose to add the warning in three places (first-steps, AsyncResult API reference, and Tasks) because the developer will likely not read them all. It could be removed from first-steps because it would be difficult for the developer to fully implement without reading at least one of Tasks or the API reference.

issue.title: Document changes in task execution options introduced in #4709
issue.body:
## Description

Pull Request #4709 introduced changes to `AsyncResult` public interface and `apply_async` task execution options. Also `AsyncResult.get()` behavior is changed for tasks with ignored result and is no longer blocking. In addition see this [comment](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues/4707#issuecomment-387283082).
